sections.heading: Why routing matters
sections.content: Different requests benefit from different models and tools. A router classifies intent and constraints (latency, cost, safety) and dispatches to: a generation model, a retrieval step, a function/tool, or a chain/agent. Good routing improves quality and efficiency.

sections.caption: Intent → Policy → Route: choose model/tools and constraints; fallback on errors or unsafe inputs.

sections.heading: Signals for routing decisions
content: Task intent: classify as generate, extract, search, transform, classify
Input size: long inputs may need retrieval or a larger context model
Latency & budget: choose a smaller/cheaper model for non‑critical tasks
Safety: if unsafe/PII detected, block or switch to a filtered flow
Domain: route to a domain‑tuned model or knowledge base

sections.heading: Router (pseudo‑JS)
Hands‑on (AgentOps Studio + API Config)
sections.description: Create a simple router that splits between: (A) Draft (generate), (B) Extract JSON (schema), (C) Search (RAG).
steps: In API Config, enable two providers: one fast and one high‑quality
In AgentOps Studio, create three nodes: generate, extract(schema) and retrieve
Add an initial node that classifies intent with a few labels
Wire routes to each node; add a fallback if the provider fails
Try three different inputs and compare accuracy/latency

options.b: Choose the best flow for each request
